description:
Programme Overview

The University of Melbourne Graduate Research Scholarships are , fully funded opportunities for high-achieving domestic and international students to pursue Master's by Research or PhD degrees at one of Australia's leading universities. For the 2026 intake, approximately 600 scholarships are available, providing comprehensive financial support to successful candidates.

Key Features

  • Fully Funded: Covers tuition, living expenses, relocation, and health insurance
  • Automatic Consideration: No separate scholarship application required
  • Open to All: Available to both domestic and international students
  • Institution: Study at Australia's #1 ranked university for graduate employability

Funding Details & Benefits

  • Tuition Fees: 100% coverage for up to 2 years (Master's by Research) or up to 4 years (PhD)
  • Living Allowance: $39,500 per year (pro rata), tax-free and indexed annually, for up to 2 years (Master's) or 3.5 years (PhD)
  • Relocation Grant: $2,000 (domestic) or $3,000 (international)
  • Health Insurance: Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for international students
  • Total Value: Up to $135,000 combined benefits
  • Limited paid sick, maternity, and parenting leave included
  • Access to research facilities and supervisors
  • Professional development and networking opportunities

Eligibility Criteria

  • Academic Admission: Have applied for and meet the entry requirements for a graduate research degree (Master's by Research or PhD) at the University of Melbourne, or be currently enrolled
  • Academic Excellence: Demonstrate a strong academic record in previous studies
  • Research Potential: Show potential for research in chosen field
  • English Proficiency: Meet the University's English language requirements
  • Visa Requirements (for international students): Be eligible for an Australian student visa

Eligible Fields of Study

All study areas at the University of Melbourne, including Agricultural and veterinary sciences, Architecture, building, planning and design, Arts, humanities and social sciences, Business and economics, Education, Engineering, Environment, Health, Information technology and computer science, Law, Music, visual and performing arts, Science.

Application Process

  1. Research available programs.
  2. Check entry requirements.
  3. Find potential supervisor (for research proposals).
  4. Prepare application documents.
  5. Submit course application before deadline.
  6. Automatic scholarship consideration (no separate application needed).
  7. Wait for outcome.

Required Documents

  • Academic Transcripts
  • Degree Certificates
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Research Proposal
  • Publications/Proof of Research Experience (if applicable)
  • English Proficiency Results (IELTS, TOEFL, or other accepted tests)
  • Passport Copy (for international applicants)
  • Supervisor Support Evidence (if required)

Key Dates & Deadlines

Selection Criteria

  1. Academic Merit: Outstanding academic results in previous studies
  2. Research Potential: Demonstrated potential for research in chosen field
  3. Research Proposal: Quality and feasibility of proposed research project
  4. Referee Reports: Strong recommendations from academic referees
  5. Publication Record: Any research publications or presentations (if applicable)

Official Application Portal

https://study.unimelb.edu.au/how-to-apply/graduate-research/international-applications/applications

Official Scholarship Page

https://scholarships.unimelb.edu.au/awards/graduate-research-scholarships

Important Notes

  • There is no separate scholarship application. You are automatically considered when you apply for your course by the closing date.
  • Current students or those who deferred must submit a separate online scholarship application by 31 October.
  • Must first apply for and be offered a place in a graduate research degree to be considered.
